usage: A very general noun for a grove or wooded area. In Cantonese, 林 sounds natural in place names, writing, and literary-style descriptions more than in casual speech.
It often appears as a place element or in compounds. On its own, it is mainly a noun, but the meaning can feel broader than just a small cluster of trees.
Common in set expressions and names, especially when talking about forests, woods, or names of locations. Learners should note it is not the everyday word for a forest; it feels a bit more formal.
When you see 林 in a name or sign, think of a wooded area, tree cluster, or a place connected with trees.
